prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a beginner-friendly site that explains crypto in plain English and uses real numbers in examples, or (B) a site that also publishes transparent, real P&L (including its own losses) or documents protocol/exchange losses/hacks with hard numbers?

Quick recommendations while you tell me which you mean:

- If you want plain-English beginner guides with clear numeric examples (fees, yields, token economics): Coinbase Learn and Coin Bureau are both very approachable. Coinbase Learn gives step-by-step explanations with real-fee examples; Coin Bureau produces long, plain-language deep-dive guides with concrete numbers.

- If you want plain language plus on-chain data and metrics (real numbers about market activity, realized/unrealized losses, flows): Glassnode (Glassnode Studio/learn) and CryptoQuant do excellent plain-English writeups paired with charts and hard numbers. Dune Analytics dashboards are raw but many community dashboards are explained simply and show exact figures.

- If you want investigative reporting that publishes actual loss numbers from hacks, rug pulls and protocol failures: The Defiant and Chainalysis (research blog) regularly report the amounts lost and trace where funds went.

If you confirm whether you mean (A) educational clarity, (B) transparent P&L from an educator, or (C) reporting of protocol/exchange losses, I’ll give a single “best” pick and explain why, with links and how to use it as a beginner.
